description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE � No. 75N98026R00175 Title: Biobanking, Laboratory Analytics, and Associated Informatics Services for NIH Biorepositories Agency: National Institutes of Health (NIH) Description This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal of abstracts or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified business sources and (2) whether commercial sources and services are available in the marketplace. Your response to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. This notice is issued to help determine the appropriate acquisition method including small business socioeconomic set aside possibilities and to determine the availability of commercial or non-commercial companies technically capable of meeting the Government's potential requirement. It is not construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Furthermore, it should be noted that any future solicitations that may be issued as a result of this notice, or in response to this requirement, may be issued using a different solicitation number from the one identified above. Purpose NIH is seeking capability statements from businesses, and subcontractors regarding their abilities to continue the work of the NIDA Center for Genetic Studies (NCGS) and the NIH Brain Development Cohorts (NBDC) Biobank, which supports the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study, and HEALthy Brain and Child Development (HBCD) Study. Background NIH currently supports over 20 biorepositories across 10+ Institutes and Centers, with each individual biorepository storing several thousands to over 3.5 million samples. NIH biorepositories have stored, analyzed, and distributed millions of samples of biomaterials to enable broad investigations into the myriad of biological and environmental factors that affect health, development, and disease. These repositories typically: Receive, process, store, and biosamples from a wide range of biospecimen types (e.g. blood/derivatives, fluids, DNA/RNA, hair, cell lines, iPSCs, teeth, fecal matter, birth specimens and other tissues such as brain and other organs) at various temperature and storage conditions (e.g. -80C, liquid nitrogen; fresh, frozen, paraffin-embedded, formalin-fixed) at scales ranging from tens of thousands to several million specimens. Serve dozens to hundreds of research studies across the United States and abroad. Enable broad, controlled-access biomaterial sharing to meet specific research objectives that further our knowledge of health Anticipate continued growth in biospecimen and data volume over the life of the award. Scope of Work & Required Capabilities Capable vendors should provide examples from current or previous projects when responding to capabilities. A. Sample Management and Storage Maintain secure, humidity- and temperature-controlled storage and tracking for at least 3,500,000 biospecimens in accordance with Best Practices, Clinical and Laboratory Standards, and Good Laboratory Practice (GLP; 21 CFR 58) with expert quality control and assurance procedures. Document the maximum capacity that could be achieved to expand storage beyond the minimum requested. Destroy samples per regulatory and consent requirements when no longer needed. College of American Pathologists (CAP) Biorepository Accreditation preferred. Maintain positive chain of custody and resolve data/sample discrepancies (missing data, incorrect information, misdirected samples) through issue tracking and resolution, coordinating with relevant receiving/data management teams (e.g. sites, site monitors, study staff). Receive de-identified clinical, diagnostic, environmental, and phenotypic data alongside biospecimens from funded grants/contracts. Centrally manage and cost-effectively distribute biosamples to qualified investigators approved through established access programs. Provide studies with collection kits and supplies, including barcoded tubes with human-readable labels. Provide research staff training for ordering supplies and collecting samples. B. Data Curation and Management Develop and maintain SOPs for sample receipt, storage, processing, QC, and distribution. Receive de-identified clinical, diagnostic, environmental, and phenotypic data associated with biospecimens from funded grants/contracts. Maintain an internal relational database (e.g., using persistent identifiers such as RRIDs) linked to associated data and participant and sample identifiers, with computerized inventory management and accurate tracking of sample and data location. Register and track biospecimens via an internal relational database with sample IDs (RRID) linked to participant IDs and associated data in the Contractor's auditable LIMS, with computerized inventory management and accurate tracking of sample/data location. Clean, standardize, and harmonize clinical data with cross-disorder phenotypic knowledge (e.g. different diagnostic systems or criteria, such as RDOC, DSM, ICD), incorporating data from electronic health records when applicable. Transfer data and sample IDs to controlled-access repositories or Data Centers (e.g., dbGAP, NBDC Data Hub or program specific data repositories). C. Laboratory and Analytic Capabilities Demonstrate laboratory expertise appropriate to the repository's sample types, which may include molecular biology techniques (e.g., DNA/RNA extraction, cell line transformation/immortalization), rigorous quality control, and tissue/cell culture (isolation, scale-up, and banking of primary cells). Provide CLIA-certification status. Provide laboratory capabilities for, but not limited to: metabolic, hematologic, and/or clinical assays high-throughput genotyping, sequencing, and gene-expression analysis Mass spectrometry for proteomics and metabolomics Advanced genomic and cellular techniques such as short- and long-range sequencing, chromatin capture, ChIP-seq, Cut-and-Tag, HiC generation of iPSC/neural stem cell lines CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing Analysis of RNA and DNA from Formalin-Fixed Parafin-Embedded tissue Provide scientific and technical expertise to evaluate and respond to researcher-submitted requests for biospecimen availability. Demonstrate that lead investigators and support staff have relevant experience in biobanking, LIMS, and database management Store and/or process histopathological tissue samples. Isolate, scale up, and bank primary cells from diverse tissue samples. D. Informatics Requirements and Cyberinfrastructure Develop, or manage and enhance (if already existing), a biorepository web portal (front-end and back-end), supporting existing features and providing updates/improvements as requested, potentially including: Synchronizing sample availability data with a public- or investigator-facing sample explorer tool to streamline discovery of related data and biospecimens across repositories Showcase published research and provide lay summaries Advertise repository resources For existing resources, support all currently available features, with updates and improvements as requested Where in scope, develop outreach tools (e.g., an integrated chatbot or public-facing portal) to help users locate biomaterials/data and discover related resources across repositories Develop or maintain backend infrastructure (e.g., server maintenance, microservices, relational databases such as PostgreSQL) and front-end website design/UI-UX. Maintain Authority to Operate (ATO) and require security documentation to keep systems compliant with appl

title: Shirley Creek Campground Improvements
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 127EAX26Q0114 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) to furnish all labor, materials, tools, transportation, and necessary supervision to perform campground improvements at Shirley Creek Campground, on the Brownstown Ranger District of the Hoosier National Forest. This project will develop individual campsites at the existing Shirley Creek Campground. Work includes staking camping spurs from plans, stripping turf, earthwork, excavating campsite spurs and social areas to sub-grade, install and compact aggregate base course, install and compact aggregate surface course, grading to ensure proper drainage around spurs and social areas, and restoring areas disturbed by construction operations with topsoil, seed and mulch. Stripped turf and excess earthen materials are to be disposed of, by the contractor, to on-site locations within the campground which will be designated by the COR. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 238910 The small business size standard is $19M This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency. title: Request for Information - Sentinel OMC Packages & OGF, Malmstrom Air Force Base, MT
description: 1. NOTICE AND DISCLAIMER This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market intelligence and acquisition planning purposes. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Qualifications (RFQ), or invitation for bid. No solicitation is currently available. Participation is strictly voluntary. The Government will not award any agreement or contract as a result of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. Submission of a response does not obligate the Government in any way and will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) or FAR-based small-business set-aside rules, the NAICS code above is provided for market-intelligence purposes to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base. 2. PURPOSE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District, is conducting market intelligence to assess industry capability, capacity, interest, and feedback regarding the potential establishment of a multi-year, multi-party Other Transaction Authority (OTA) framework agreement under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The framework would enable Seattle District to execute a multitude of OTA methods with multiple parties over numerous years, with individual projects or packages authorized through project orders. While the near-term primary focus is the Sentinel Operations and Maintenance Complex (OMC) packages (OMC includes Consolidated Maintenance Facility, Integrated Training Center, Missile Handling Center, and Integrated Command Center) and Operations Group Facility (OGF) at Malmstrom Air Force Base, the Government is also interested in industry feedback on a vehicle broad enough to support construction of numerous facilities at military installations under Seattle District�s area of responsibility. 3. PROJECT BACKGROUND � PRIMARY NEAR-TERM FOCUS The Sentinel (Ground Based Strategic Deterrent) program is modernizing the Nation�s land-based intercontinental ballistic missile force. At Malmstrom AFB, the Air Force is constructing a suite of new facilities collectively referred to as the OMC, together with the OGF. These facilities replace aging Minuteman III infrastructure and provide purpose-built command, maintenance, training, missile-handling, and operations capabilities for the Sentinel weapon system. Primary near-term facilities under consideration include (approximate sizes based on current planning data; final designs may vary): Consolidated Maintenance Facility (CMF) (Est. Magnitude: $200M-$300M) � Approximately 181,000 SF. Administrative offices, maintenance shops, drive-thru high bays with overhead cranes and vehicle exhaust systems sized for Transporter Erectors (TE), Payload Transporters (PT), and Missile Transporters (MT); vault and secure storage; loading dock and shipping/receiving areas. Integrated Training Center (ITC) (Est. Magnitude: $100M-$200M) � Approximately 77,000 SF. High-bay and single-story technical training labs, shops, and classrooms consolidating wing-level maintenance, security forces, cyber-defense, and operations training on Sentinel-unique systems and devices. Missile Handling Complex (MHC)(Est. Magnitude: $100M-$200M) � Two facilities totaling approximately 50,000 SF. Three-bay transfer facility with embedded rails for Sentinel missile handling and a companion three-bay facility for positioning and storage of mission-ready transporters/erectors. Integrated Command Center (ICC)(Est. Magnitude: $100M-$200M) � Centralized operations facility supporting day-to-day mission control, status and security monitoring, weapons-systems management, cyber defense, and real-time leadership situational awareness. Operations Group Facility (OGF)(Est. Magnitude: $200M-$300M) � Multi-story office and collaboration space supporting planning and operations functions, enhancing span of control, and providing associated support spaces (administrative, training, supply, and dispatch functions). Design for these packages is being performed by Jacobs Engineering under existing design contracts. Design maturity varies by package (35% to 95%, with a majority at 95% completion). The Air Force treats the OMC as one project under a single aggregated DD Form 1391. Utility Infrastructure, which serves the entire OMC campus, is currently being addressed under a separate OT method. (See Sam.gov Notice ID: W912DW26S1CE0, Title: Request for Information - Sentinel Utility Infrastructure, Malmstrom Air Force Base, MT). 4. POTENTIAL ACQUISITION STRATEGY � FRAMEWORK CONCEPT Seattle District is exploring the feasibility of establishing one large overarching Other Transaction agreement (or a limited number of agreements) under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a that would function as a flexible multi-year framework. Key characteristics under consideration include: Multi-year period of performance sufficient to support sequential and concurrent facility packages across the Sentinel beddown and related MILCON workload. It is anticipated to be approximately 5 years with the potential to extend to a total of 7 years. Multiple parties � Potential for single-agreement or multiple-agreement structure allowing the Government to select among qualified parties for individual project/sub-agreement opportunities. Multitude of OTA methods � Flexibility to apply Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk), Progressive Design-Build, construction-only collaborative approaches, or other commercially adapted methods on a project-by-project basis depending on design maturity, risk profile, and schedule drivers. Project orders � Individual work packages or scopes would be authorized through bilateral project orders that define scope, price (or GMP), schedule, and method, analogous to task/project orders under an overarching agreement. Geographic and mission flexibility � While Malmstrom Sentinel packages (OMC and OGF) are the immediate focus, the framework is considering the possibility/capability for other MILCON workload assigned to Seattle District (anticipated to cover areas across Washington, Montana, Idaho, and Oregon. Military Installations include but are not limited to: Malmstrom Air Force Base, Fairchild Air Force Base, Mountain Home Air Force Base, Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Air National Guard Sites). The Government seeks industry input on whether this type of multi-party, multi-method, multi-year OT framework is attractive and executable, what commercial terms would make it successful, and how best to structure competition, on-ramping, and project order competition or selection. 5. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Interested parties are requested to submit responses by completing the online questionnaire at https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/dnW9AUb6aj The questionnaire is the Government's primary mechanism for obtaining detailed market intelligence and addresses industry capability, experience, technical capabilities, construction considerations, and recommended OTA and commercial practices. If necessary, interested parties may also submit a brief capabilities statement containing relevant information not otherwise addressed in the questionnaire. Capability statements shall not exceed 5 pages in length. The Government requests that firms avoid duplicating information already provided through the questionnaire. Supplemental capability statements are requested to be submitted via email to the individual(s) listed below no later than 10:00 AM Pacific Time on 20 October 2026. Late responses may still be considered at the Government�s discretion but are not guaranteed review prior to strategy finalization. title: Design-Bid-Build (DBB) SOF Marine Raider Facilities Complex, Marine Corps Base (MCB) Camp Lejeune, North Carolina
description: The general intent of this solicitation is to award a Fixed Price Construction Contract for a Design-Bid-Build (DBB), construction services for the P-1550 SOF Marine Raider Battalion Company & Team Facilities located at the Marine Corps Base in Camp Lejeune in North Carolina. The project is to provide construction of 6,815 SM (73,400 SF) SOF Marine Battalion Operations, Supply, Communications, and Intel facility; 11,812 SM (127,200 SF) Company HQ and Team Facilities; 1,635 SM (17,600 SF) Company Storage Buildings and miscellaneous supporting structures, utilities, parking, roadways, pedestrian ways/sidewalks, and site work at Stone Bay at the Marine Corps Base (MCB) in Camp Lejeune, North Carolina. The structures will be single-story steel frame buildings with brick veneer over metal studs, standing seam metal roofs, metal soffits, and translucent wall panels. Special construction features include pile foundations, surcharged sites, wetlands mitigation, and storm water best management practices.

title: L099--On-Site Inscription Services at Fort Snelling National Cemetery - MPS
description: On-Site Inscription Services at Fort Snelling National Cemetery - MPS The purpose of this amendment is to address submitted questions and provide additional information. A revised Combined Synopsis/Solicitation (CSS) and revised Attachment F Drawings are provided. The revised CSS includes updates and clarifications to the sample requirements and inscriptions. Attachment F Drawings has been revised to include the Emblems of Belief document. The response due date and time remains 20 October 2026 at 1:00 p.m. CT. Note: There will not be a SF30 to sign for this amendment. Quoters shall provide a statement of acknowledgement and receipt of any and all amendments. Failure to acknowledge all amendments may result in the Interested Quoter being considered non-responsive and ineligible for award. Clarification Reverse (R2) Inscriptions: The unit price for U1, V1, W1, and other applicable upright headstones is all-inclusive when the front and reverse inscriptions are ordered together. A separate R2 line item shall not be charged in that circumstance. The R2 line item applies only when a reverse inscription is ordered separately on an existing upright headstone with a previously completed front inscription. Questions and Answers: Q: May samples submitted under previous solicitations be used to satisfy the sample requirements for the current open solicitations if those samples were previously approved by MPS? A: No. Samples submitted under previous solicitations do not apply to the current solicitations, and there is no provision to carry forward prior sample approvals. New samples shall be submitted in accordance with the requirements of the current solicitations. Q: Is there any incumbent/recompete or this is a brand-new project? If yes, could you please provide us with their award number or even if the customer bought similar services in the past? A: This requirement is a recompete. Information regarding prior awards is publicly available on SAM.gov. Quoters shall prepare quotations based on the requirements of the current solicitation. Q: Ktr 1: The solicitation permits use of a subcontractor s past performance with a teaming agreement but also requires the prime contractor s own past performance relating to the required service. May a prime contractor without prior onsite inscription contracts submit an acceptable quotation using a qualified inscription subcontractor s relevant experience, references, key personnel, and samples under a teaming agreement? If so, what past performance information must the prime provide? Ktr 2: Factors 1 and 2 permit subcontractor past performance with a teaming agreement but also require the prime s own relevant past-performance information. Is prior on-site inscription experience mandatory at the prime-company level, or may a prime without its own inscription history be considered using its other relevant contract-management experience together with the subcontractor s inscription references and qualified personnel? How would the prime s lack of inscription-specific past performance be evaluated? Ktr 3: Past performance: Can a prime without its own inscription past performance be considered when it submits a signed teaming agreement with an experienced inscription subcontractor? A: The Government will not make a prospective determination regarding the acceptability of a proposed teaming arrangement or quote. Quoters may use a subcontractor s past performance only if a teaming agreement is provided with the quote. However, the Prime Contractor must provide its own past performance information as required by Factor 2. A subcontractor s experience, past performance, key personnel, or samples do not relieve the Prime Contractor of any requirements applicable to the Prime Contractor under Factors 1 and 2 or the SOW, including, but not limited to, SOW Section 19.0. Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with the stated evaluation criteria. Q: Ktr 1: The solicitation uses CST, while SAM.gov lists the quote deadline as 1:00 p.m. CDT on October 20, 2026. Please confirm that the questions deadline is September 30 at 3:00 p.m. Chicago local time and that the quotation and physical samples deadline is October 20 at 1:00 p.m. Chicago local time. Ktr 2: Please confirm whether quotations and physical samples are due October 20 at 1:00 PM CDT; the solicitation document states CST. A: Quotes and physical samples are due October 20, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. Central Time (CT). The Combined Synopsis/Solicitation has been revised accordingly. Q: Ktr 1: Please identify the applicable limitations on subcontracting and prime self-performance requirements, including how performance by a similarly situated small-business subcontractor would be treated and documented. Ktr 2: Prime staffing: Does SOW §19(b) require the stated 50% salaries/wages share to be paid to the prime s direct employees, or can work by a similarly situated small-business subcontractor count under FAR 52.219-14? A: Quoters are responsible for reviewing and complying with all applicable solicitation and SOW requirements, including, but not limited to, FAR 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, and SOW Section 19.0. Q: May the identified inscription subcontractor manufacture and inscribe the required samples for QLC s submission? If so, please confirm any identification or documentation requirements beyond those stated in the solicitation. A: The solicitation does not require the samples to be manufactured or inscribed by the Prime Contractor. However, use of a subcontractor does not relieve the Prime Contractor of compliance with any solicitation or SOW requirements, including, but not limited to, SOW Section 19.0. Samples shall comply with all identification, submission, and evaluation requirements stated in the solicitation. Q: The SOW requires setup within 25 calendar days of award, while the base period begins April 1, 2027. Please clarify the required mobilization and service-start dates if award occurs before that date. A: The 25 calendar day setup period begins on the contract effective date. The anticipated contract effective date and base period start date is April 1, 2027. Execution of the contract prior to the effective date does not begin the setup period.

description: The general intent of this solicitation is to award a Fixed Price Construction Contract for a Design-Bid-Build (DBB), construction services for the P-1550 SOF Marine Raider Battalion Company & Team Facilities located at the Marine Corps Base in Camp Lejeune in North Carolina. The project is to provide construction of 6,815 SM (73,400 SF) SOF Marine Battalion Operations, Supply, Communications, and Intel facility; 11,812 SM (127,200 SF) Company HQ and Team Facilities; 1,635 SM (17,600 SF) Company Storage Buildings and miscellaneous supporting structures, utilities, parking, roadways, pedestrian ways/sidewalks, and site work at Stone Bay at the Marine Corps Base (MCB) in Camp Lejeune, North Carolina. The structures will be single-story steel frame buildings with brick veneer over metal studs, standing seam metal roofs, metal soffits, and translucent wall panels. title: SOURCES SOUGHT: Carters Reregulation Dam Short Term Repairs
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS and is not a solicitation announcement. The purpose of this Market Research and Sources Sought Notice is to gain knowledge of potential qualified Small Business, HUBZone, 8(a), Service Disabled Veteran owned, and Women owned Small Business firms. Responses to this Sources Sought Synopsis will be used by the government in making appropriate acquisition decisions. The intended work falls under NAICS code 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Mobile District, anticipates a requirement for a firm-fixed-price construction contract to perform structural concrete and gate repairs on the spillway at the Carters Reregulation Dam located in Chatsworth, Georgia. The purpose of this project is to perform concrete rehabilitation and retrofit existing structural elements that have been impacted by concrete expansion due to Alkali-Silica Reactivity (ASR). The scope of work includes, but is not limited to: structural concrete demolition of existing pier stoplog slots; installation of new steel stoplog guides and embedded seal plates; placement of specialized shrinkage-compensating concrete; and recessing of side seal plates. Additional mechanical and structural work includes replacing side and bottom seals on four (4) Tainter gates and replacing seals on eight (8) stop logs. The contractor will be fully responsible for the design, fabrication, and installation of Temporary Dewatering Structures (TDS)/cofferdams and temporary gate support shoring. To maintain operational continuity, construction must be executed sequentially, allowing only one gate bay to be dewatered and out of service at any given time. The estimated magnitude of construction is between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000, with an anticipated performance period of approximately 180 calendar days. Responses are requested with the following information, which shall not exceed a total of eight pages. 1. Offeror name, address, points of contact with telephone numbers and e-mail addresses. 2. Business size/classification to include any designations as Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, Service Disabled Veteran Owned and Women-Owned Small Businesses shall be indicated on first page of submission. 3. Bonding capability: construction bonding level per single contract and aggregate construction bonding level, both expressed in dollars; along with current available bonding capacity. 4. Description of your capability to perform the specialized work described above, manage subcontractors, secure and comply with environmental permits, and safely execute Dam and hydraulic Steel structures (HSS) construction. Specifically address your capacity and proposed approach to designing, fabricating, and installing Temporary Dewatering Structures (TDS) and tainter gate shoring systems. 5. Past performance and experience on up to three (3) projects of similar scope, complexity, and value completed within the past five (5) years, or at least 50% construction complete. Relevant experience includes: structural concrete demolition, specialized concrete placement (such as shrinkage-compensating concrete under strict curing/testing protocols), stainless steel structural embed/guide fabrication and welding, Tainter gate seal replacement, and work with USACE Hydraulic Steel Structures within the civil works branch. For each project, provide the title, location, general description of the scope, contract value, role (Prime or Subcontractor), and client contact information (name, phone, and email). NO RESPONSES WILL BE ACCEPTED BY FAX OR MAIL. ALL RESPONSES MUST BE E-MAILED to: Jeffrey M. Donaldson at Jeffrey.M.Donaldson@usace.army.mil. Submittals are due no later than 20 October 2026 at 2:00 PM CDT. Telephonic responses will not be honored. This is not a Request for Proposal, only a Request for Information. No award will result from this Sources Sought. This notice does not constitute any commitment by the Government.

description: 75H70127R00001 Sources Sought: Fort Yates Pharmacy USP Renovation in Fort Yates, ND. The Indian Health Service (IHS) is conducting a SOURCES SOUGHT/REQUEST FOR INFORMATION as outlined in FAR 15.201(c)(3) to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities, and qualifications of firms especially small businesses including: Native American/Indian-Owned Businesses (Indian Economic Enterprise (IEE)), 8(a) Certified Small Businesses, Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUB-Zone) Small Businesses, Women Owned Small Businesses, Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), Small Disadvantaged Businesses (SDB), and Veteran Owned Small Businesses. NO PROPOSALS ARE BEING REQUESTED OR ACCEPTED WITH THIS RFI. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS. Respondents will NOT be notified of the results of this notice. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this notice or any follow-up information requested. Market Research is being performed pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 to identify businesses capable of performing the functions described herein. SUMMARY OF SCOPE This project is to renovate and reconfigure the existing inpatient and outpatient pharmacy spaces within the Fort Yates Hospital while maintaining continuous pharmacy operations throughout construction. The work will be performed in phases to minimize disruption to hospital services, with any required shutdowns coordinated in advance with the COR and service unit. The project will first renovate an existing hospital area to serve as a temporary outpatient pharmacy and relocate the necessary pharmacy equipment, shelving, narcotics cage and vault, refrigerators/freezers, and ScriptPro robot. The existing outpatient pharmacy will then be renovated to include a break room, office, consultation room, dispensing area, receiving/hazardous drug storage room, narcotics area, and pharmacy work area. Upon completion, equipment and operations will be relocated from the temporary space to the newly renovated outpatient pharmacy. The temporary outpatient pharmacy area will subsequently be renovated into a new inpatient pharmacy and future physical therapy area, while the existing inpatient pharmacy will be converted into nursing, medical, and sterile storage rooms. description: 2 ` EXPRESSION OF INTEREST VA Outpatient Clinic (VAOC), New Philadelphia, Ohio 36C25027R0016 The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Seeks Expressions of Interest for approximately 15,000 American National Standards Institute/Building Owners and Managements Association (ANSI/BOMA) Square Feet (ABOA SF) in New Philadelphia, Ohio. Notice: This advertisement is an advertisement of a potential opportunity. This advertisement is not a solicitation for offers, nor is it a request for proposals. The Government will not pay for any costs incurred because of this advertisement. Contracting Officer Address: Brian Walton Brian.Walton@va.gov Lease Contracting Officer CFM-Minor Leasing U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Description: VA seeks to lease approximately 15,000 ABOA SF of office and medical space; and 100 surface parking spaces, for use by the VA as an Outpatient Clinic in the delineated area outlined within New Philadelphia, Ohio, below. VA will consider leased space in existing buildings, new construction, or a building being constructed for multi-tenant use and not specifically a build-to-suit for VA only use. Lease Term: Up to 20-Years*** ***Site must be able to support municipal water and sewer utilities. Delineated Area: In order to receive consideration, submitted properties must be located within the following area outlined below, which is bounded by the following roads, or must front on any of the following boundary lines: Northern Boundary: Mt. Pleasant Road; Columbia Road; North Wooster Ave. Extended NW; North Wooster Ave.; South Wooster Ave.; East Iron Ave.; Boulevard St.; 4th St. NW (Rt 800); 2nd St. NE; East High Ave.; Eastern Boundary: North Wooster Ave. Extended NW; North Wooster Ave.; South Wooster Ave.; East Iron Ave.; Boulevard St.; 4th St. NW (Rt 800); 2nd St. NE; East High Ave. Southern Boundary; Route 250; Western Boundary: Route 77. Additional Requirements: Site must be able to support municipal water and sewer utility services. Be located on a single contiguous floor; Bifurcated sites, inclusive of parking, are not permissible; The following space configurations will not be considered: Space with atriums or other areas interrupting contiguous space, extremely long or narrow runs of space (more than twice as long as wide), irregularly shaped space configurations or other unusual building features adversely affecting usage; Offered space cannot be in the FEMA 1-percent-annual-chance flood; Offered space must be zoned for VA s intended use; Offered space will not be considered if located in close proximity to property with incompatible uses, including but not limited to the following uses: liquor establishments, dispensaries, treatment centers, correctional facilities, where firearms are sold/discharged, railroad tracks, industrial areas, residential developments; or within flight paths; Space will not be considered where apartment space or other living quarters are located within the same building; Offered space must be located in close proximity to amenities including but not limited to restaurants, hotels, pharmacy, and shopping; Offered space must be located in close proximity to a hospital or stand-alone emergency room center and a fire department; Offered space must be located in close proximity to public transportation. A commuter rail, light rail, or bus stop shall be located within the immediate vicinity of the building; Offered space must be easily accessible to multiple highways which provide multiple routes of travel; Loading dock or loading area with a roll up door is required. The parking lot must be able to accommodate deliveries by semi-trucks with trailers; Structured parking under the space is not permissible; Offered space must meet Federal and Local Government requirements for fire safety, physical security, accessibility, seismic, and sustainability standards per the terms of the formal request for proposals (pending issuance); A fully serviced lease is required; Offered space must be compatible for VA s intended use; Space must not have any environmental issues or hazards; Must meet Government requirements for fire safety, accessibility, seismic, and sustainability standards per the terms of the Lease. To be considered for a Market Survey, all expressions of interest submissions must include the following information, if applicable, by the expression of interest due date, infra: Property Owner (or representative) contact information (name, phone number, and email); Evidence the owner/representative has the authority to represent the property owner; Building address or address of the geographical location of the land; Provide a map demonstrating the building or land parcel lied within the required delineated area; A description of ingress/egress to the building or land from a public right-of-way; Description of the uses of adjacent properties; Evidence of ABBAS compliance or stated willingness to upgrade; A site plan depicting the property boundaries, building, parking, and amenities; Provide clear demonstration of the RSF and ABOA being offered under the submission; Provide descriptions of any changes to the property that might be necessary for compliance with the VA s intended use. Provide a statement and supporting documentation, if applicable, which demonstrates any environmental and/or cultural/historic studies applicable to the property (e.g. Phase I or Phase II ESAs, NEPA environmental assessments, or historical/archaeological surveys). Set Aside Determination: Any qualified Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) under NAICS Code 531120 {Lessors of Non-residential Buildings); with the associated small business size standard; your entity must meet the requirements outlined in the attachment titled: SDVOSB, VOSB, or JV Status , and submit the required certification information to the Lease Contracting Officer with any expression of interest submission. If you are a Joint Venture (JV) and intend to submit an offer as such; JV s must submit evidence of verification in the attachment titled: SDVOSB, VOSB, or JV Status , and submit the required certification information to the Lease Contracting Officer with any expression of interest submission. (to include: JV s certification status as a legal SDVOSB entity; a copy of your JV agreement {a UEI number in the JV name, CAGE code number for the JV, and evidence of a proper JV agreement being in place}). If your entity does not meet the JV requirements outlined by the Small Business Association (SBA) and the new Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) by the close of the expression of interest due date, the submission will not considered incomplete, and JV status will not be considered. Expression of Interest Due Date: All interested parties must respond to this announcement, and provide the required documentation under their submissions, no later than October 20, 2026, at 3:00pm ET. Expression of Interest Submission Format: All submissions must be sent via email to Brian Walton at, brian.walton@va.gov. Market Survey: The estimated Market Survey date is late October 2026.

As part of this mission, the Marine Forces Storage Command (MFSC) CSM Program provides logistical augmentation to the Marine Corps Reparable Issue Point(s) (RIP) located at I, II, and III MEF, as well as MFR in support of the CSM program, which is detailed in MCO 4400.200A. Additionally, the MFSC CSM Program performs strategic level CPI in consonance with the Logistics Modernization Solution Initiating Directive (LSMID) that outlines anticipated Realignment of Supply (ROS) outcomes for SECREP management. title: 6130--Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) for Pharmaceutical Refrigerators
description: SOURCE SOUGHT NOTICE - Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) for VA Medical Clinic This announcement requests information from industry to support market research and preliminary acquisition planning for the procurement described below. The purpose of this notice is to assess industry interest and identify potential sources with the capabilities and qualifications to meet the following requirements. This is not a solicitation for proposals. No contract will be awarded from this notice. No proposals are being requested or accepted with this notice. REQUIREMENT The agency is seeking information on domestic sources of supply for two types of Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) backups with salient characteristics described below: Type One Quantity 3 ea. Shall have at least 2000 Watts Output Shall have minimum surge capacity of 4,000 watts Made in America Must include at least 2 120V NEMA 5-20 duplex receptacles Dimensions cannot exceed be 91 H X 14 W X 10 D ±6 , in any direction Shall have single-phase 120 VAC, 60 Hz output Shall be capable of providing 88 hours of running time for a single half-size pharmaceutical refrigerator Shall be designed for operation in healthcare environments Automatic backup power activation transfer time shall be less than 20 milliseconds Shall be designed for indoor installation Must be capable of being wall mounted due to space limitations in the medication alcoves Shall provide a pure sine wave output suitable for medical-grade refrigeration, electronic controls, monitoring systems, and other sensitive healthcare equipment. Shall operate from a standard 120 VAC, 20-amp utility circuit and shall utilize a NEMA 5-20P connection or equivalent. Type Two Quantity 1 ea. Shall have at least 3000 Watts Output (Qty = 1) Shall have minimum surge capacity of 6,000 watts Made in America Must include at least 2 120V NEMA 5-20 duplex receptacles Dimensions cannot exceed 91 H X 55 W X 10 D ±6 any direction Shall have single-phase 120 VAC, 60 Hz output Shall be capable of providing 88 hours of running time for a single full-size pharmaceutical refrigerator Shall be designed for operation in healthcare environments Automatic backup power activation transfer time shall be less than 20 milliseconds Shall be designed for indoor installation Shall provide a pure sine wave output suitable for medical-grade refrigeration, electronic controls, monitoring systems, and other sensitive healthcare equipment. Shall operate from a standard 120 VAC, 20-amp utility circuit and shall utilize a NEMA 5-20P connection or equivalent. Interested parties who can provide the products described are requested to submit the following information: Company name, address and point of contact with phone number, SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), Product information documenting salient characteristics, Socio-economic status to identify the business class as a large business, SDVOSB, VOSB, small business, Woman Owned, etc., Place of manufacture, Any other pertinent company documentation. Note: All interested parties must be registered in SAM (System for Award Management) to be eligible for the award of a Government contract. Send submissions via email to Brian.Rosciszewski@VA.gov., reference 36C25027Q0037 is email subject. Firms that respond to this Sources Sought notice but do not provide ALL the requested information may not be considered by the Government when making acquisition decisions. This market research is for informational and planning purposes. This is not a solicitation and does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation. Please be advised that the government will not pay any costs for responses and information submitted. Respondents may not be notified of the results of this notice; it is at the discretion of the Government to release any results. ** End of Sources Sought Notice **

title: Hoisting & Rigging Equipment Support Services
description: Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory is looking to acquires PPPL personnel perform much of the routine required inspections; however, during peak workload periods and for large repairs, the Subcontractor may be called upon on to perform these tasks. This SOW provides the requirements for subcontracted periodic inspections. It also addresses the assignment to a Subcontractor of the requirement to perform remedial (corrective) maintenance, which may be determined necessary based upon the periodic inspections, in order to make a piece of equipment operable in accordance with governing codes and standards, and the performance of routine maintenance as recommended by the various equipment manufacturers. Unless specified and agreed to otherwise in writing, PPPL requires that the work be performed in accordance with the manufacturer specifications and procedures. After any maintenance is performed, a complete thorough check of equipment function shall be performed including all safety features and interlocks as described by the manufacturer. Additionally, the Subcontractor may be called upon for advice for crane upgrades and performance enhancements. Several large cranes (Items 3, 13, 33, 34 on Attachment A) are retrofitted with Catron/Electromotive radio remote controls and Variable Frequency Drives. Familiarity with and qualification in maintenance and adjustments of these cranes and control systems is mandatory. Subcontractor's membership in the Crane Manufacturers Association of America (CMAA) is regarded as highly desirable, and a measure of the Subcontractor's professionalism and technical qualification for performing tasks such as assigned under the Statement of Work.PPPL does not guarantee any minimum level of work and reserves the right to use other sources to perform the inspection and maintenance tasks when PPPL determines this to be appropriate A mandatory preproposal zoom meeting has been scheduled for 1:30 PM on 8 Oct 2026. description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE F35 3-BAY HANGAR for ROYAL SINGAPORE AIR FORCE (RSAF) EBBING AIR NATIONAL GUARD BASE (ANGB) FORT SMITH, ARKANSAS This is a PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE for the construction of a F35 3-Bay Hangar for the Royal Singapore Air Force (RSAF) at Ebbing ANGB, Fort Smith, AR. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SYNOPSIS. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this synopsis or any follow up information requests. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers � Tulsa District has been tasked to solicit for and award a F35 3-Bay Hangar for the Royal Singapore Air Force (RSAF) at Ebbing ANGB, Fort Smith, AR. The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed price contract procured in accordance with RFO 15, Negotiated Procurement using the trade-off process. This will be an unrestricted procurement that will result in the award of one (1) contract. Project Description: The work includes construction of an 3-Bay Aircraft Maintenance Hangar for the Singapore F-35 program and incidental related work. Project includes a two-story steel framed reinforced concrete aircraft hangar with a slab on grade foundation and a membrane roof system. The hangar will provide bay spaces for Aircraft Maintenance, Aircraft Corrosion Control, and Aircraft Fuel Systems Maintenance, storage areas for wash equipment and a radar verification system, storage rooms for Singapore-unique AME as well as warehouse-type space for Singapore-unique supply storage, office/admin, shop and unique support space for the F-35 Autonomic Logistics Information System (ALIS), a centralized tool room for Singapore-specific tools and support section, compressed air room, bathrooms, electrical, mechanical and telecommunication spaces and a janitor closet. The estimated construction price range for this project is $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. Estimated duration of the project is 1215 calendar days. The North American Industry Classification System code for this procurement is 236220, which has a small business size standard of $45M. TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: NONE � This requirement will be procured as unrestricted. The anticipated solicitation issuance date is on or about 20 October 2026 and the estimated proposal due date will be on or about 6 January 2027. The official solicitation will be issued under SAM.gov via PIEE.eb.mil.

title: CO NP ROMO 407(1) Holzwarth Culvert
description: SOLICITATION ID: 6982AF27B000004 PROJECT NUMBER: CO FTNP ROMO 407(1) PROJECT NAME: Holzwarth Culvert PROJECT DESCRIPTION: This project will replace the deficient Holzwarth Culvert (Structure No. 1520-029S), a six-barrel corrugated metal arch pipe culvert on the Holzwarth Access Road with a steel girder bridge. Located in Rocky Mountain National Park, approximately nine miles north of Grand Lake, CO, along US HWY 34 at an elevation of 8,900 feet, the culvert conveys flow from the Colorado River and provides access to the Holzwarth Historic Site. The purpose of this project is to prevent future roadway damage and flooding while maintaining access to employee housing, the historic site, and National Park Service and Forest Service recreation opportunities. SCOPE OF THE WORK: The project will consist of removal of the existing six barrel culvert and construction of a new steel girder bridge with a cast in place concrete deck. New bridge abutments and micropiles. Temporary stream diversion and riprap. New aggregate roadway surfacing. Relocation of an existing electrical line. Relocation of existing historic head gates into a new concrete slab. The site is accessible on foot a quarter mile past the locked gate at the south end of the Holzwarth Historic Site Parking Lot and along the Holzwarth Culvert Access Road. The Holzwarth Culvert Access Road is approximately 13� wide with tight turns. Temporary widening will be necessary to prevent truck off tracking on to sensitive environmental resources. A temporary truck turnaround will also be necessary as no construction access is allowed more than 100� west of the bridge. The Government shall ensure all procurements are awarded without jeopardizing quality or safety of flight. Only the use of airworthy commercial specifications or standard military specifications/military standard parts will be utilized and approved from this solicitation. Newly manufactured commercial items will only be procured from sources able to provide a Certificate of Conformance (COC) and traceability to the OEM. title: Request for Interested Manufacturers of 6130-01-523-3338 Power Control Module (PCM) and 1095-01-523-5767 High Bandwidth Assembly (HBA) for the Bomb Release Unit (BRU)-57
description: SUBJECT Market research is being conducted to identify potential sources that may possess the expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet the requirements for qualification and production of the Power Control Module (PCM), NSN 6130-01-523-3338, Part Number MT57M1177-1 and High Bandwidth Assembly (HBA), NSN 1095-01-523-5767, Part Number MT57M1165-1. ITEM DESCRIPTION The PCM and HBA are components of the BRU-57/A (BRU- Bomb Release Unit) Smart Bomb Rack used on the F-16 Fighter. The PCM serves as the primary electrical power management, conditioning, and distribution hub for the BRU-57/A Smart Bomb Rack system. The HBA is the communication link for the BRU-57 bomb rack. It routes high-speed data between the F-16 and two smart weapons. The BRU-57/A PCM and HBA were developed specifically for use on the F-16 C/D aircraft with military unique requirements. The BRU-57/A is a MIL-STD-1760 capable, multiple-carriage, vertical-ejection Bomb Rack. The BRU-57/A provides side-by-side carriage and release of two 14-inch suspension stores. IMPEDIMENT TO COMPETITION The original equipment manufacturer for this item is L3Harris (CAGE 82340) previously EDO LLC. The Government does not own any data, drawings, schematics, or any other releasable technical data in support of this requirement. As a result, L3Harris is the only known source with adequate knowledge of the BRU-57 performance requirements and possession of the required technical data and capabilities needed to produce these items and ensure compatibility of the equipment. INTEREST The DLA/AWB Contracting Office intends to award a sole source contract to L3 Harris for the manufacture of the BRU-57 PCM and HBA in support of the F-16C/D program. Other interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement no later than 20 October 2026, 1700 EST by emailing robert.berg.9@us.af.mil. The Government intends to procure these items using Other Than Full and Open Competition as prescribed by RFO 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. DISCLAIMER This sources sought synopsis is for informational purposes only. This is not a request for proposal. It does not constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the government. Responses in any form are not offers, and the government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. No funds are available to pay for preparation of responses to this announcement. Any information submitted by respondents to this technical description is strictly voluntary.

In addition, this market research is to determine if there are respondents that qualify under one or more socio-economic indicators, including but not limited to, small business, woman-owned business, Women Owned Small business (WOSB), Economically Disadvantaged Women Owned Small business (EDWOSB), Veteran Owned Small business, Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small business, SBA Certified Small Disadvantaged business, SBA Certified 8(a) Firm, SBA Certified HUBZone Firm. The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) anticipates procuring the services of multiple contractors to perform Flexible Coworking Services, either as shared co-working spaces (Standard coworking spaces where an organization shares the space with other individuals and organizations) or private co-working spaces (Coworking spaces where a certain area (floor, section, private offices with locks) is dedicated to a single organization for federal agencies looking to occupy a coworking space with other federal or private sector employees. It is the intention of GSA to award a multiple contractor, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. The firm shall have an online booking system where Government employees can quickly select a workspace from an online system and/or from a mobile phone application. In addition to having access to both private and shared offices and workstations, Government employees should be able to utilize a meeting room on an hourly or daily basis. The space should be able, if necessary, to be segregated from certain parts of the vendor�s general operations, or at times operate autonomously. The firm shall provide management for each location. Management duties include, but are not limited to providing, uninterrupted internet, office support, oversight for the online booking platform, monthly usage reports to GSA, and billing based on actual usage. title: McMurdo PENGUIN Ground Station Antennas and Radomes
description: INTRODUCTION SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is issued for information and market research planning purposes; it does not constitute a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) is not seeking proposals at this time, but strictly the information requested, herein. Requests for a solicitation or proposals sent in response to this notice will not receive a response. Furthermore, those who respond to this SSN should not anticipate feedback with regards to its submission. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. The information provided in this SSN is subject to change and does not bind the Government to any future obligations. All submissions become the property of the Government and will not be returned. SUMMARY OF SCOPE The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service (NESDIS), under the Office of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Observations and the Near Earth Orbit Network (NEON) / NOAA Antenna as a Service (NAaaS) program, is seeking industry capabilities and feedback regarding the procurement, fabrication, factory integration, testing, packaging, and sustainment of (5) receive-only satellite ground station systems for the PENGUIN Ground Stations project at McMurdo Station, Antarctica. See Attachment 1: McMurdo PENGUIN Ground Stations - Statement of Work for detailed scope of work information. PENGUIN Ground Station Overview Within NESDIS, the Office of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Observations maintains long-standing partnerships that support the acquisition, transport, processing, and distribution of environmental satellite data. These partnerships include cooperation with the European Organization for the Exploitation of Meteorological Satellites under the JPSS Program and are expected to expand to support the European Organization for the Exploitation of Meteorological Satellites (EUMETSAT) Polar System Second Generation (EPS-SG) constellation of microwave sounders. McMurdo Station, Antarctica, provides a strategic high-latitude location for polar-orbiting satellite data acquisition. At approximately 77.8 degrees south latitude, McMurdo enables frequent access to polar-orbiting satellites and supports Stored Mission Data downlink opportunities for NOAA and partner mission satellites. Additional receive-only ground station capability at McMurdo is required to maintain continuity, resiliency, and growth capability for NOAA environmental data acquisition architecture. The receive-only antenna and radome systems procured under this effort are expected to support known near-term mission needs, including EPS-Sterna L-band data acquisition at McMurdo. The Sterna L-band mission baseline includes Stored Mission Data (SMD) reception. The delivered antenna system is expected to include installed L-, S-, and X-band receive hardware capability. NOAA/NAaaS will establish S-band and X-band performance and interface specifications to support future mission requirements; these parameters are identified in the procurement technical specification. KEY ASSUMPTIONS AND RESPONSE INFORMATION Period of Performance: Base Period: 2 March 2027 � 1 March 2028 Option Period 1: 2 March 2028 � 1 March 2029 Locations: Performance of this work shall be conducted at the contractor�s facility. Delivery is expected to be made to the Government-designated logistics handoff point, currently Port Hueneme, California. NAICS and Size Standard: The Government contemplates the use of the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code: 334220- Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing, with the corresponding small business size standard of 1,250 employees. This is an open Sources Sought for all interested parties regardless of size, small businesses are encouraged to respond. The Government accepts recommendations for alternative NAICS codes. If a recommendation is provided, please provide the rationale for any code applicable to the planned acquisition other than the NAICS code identified above. Required Response Information: Interested Contractors are required to provide the following information in response to this Sources Sought Notice announcement: Company Name/Division, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone number, facsimile number, and website URL (if available). A single Point-of-Contact name, title, telephone number, and e-mail address. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code, Tax Identification Number (TIN), and company structure (Corporation, LLC, partnership, joint venture, etc.). Please note that companies must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to be considered potential sources (https://www.sam.gov). Business Size (regardless of company size) and any socio-economic status, especially those qualified as one or more of the following: Small Business. 8(a) firm (must be certified by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA). Small Disadvantaged Business (must be certified by the SBA). Woman-Owned Small Business. Economically Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business. HUBZone firm (must be certified by the (SBA). Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (must be listed in the VetBiz Vendor Information pages). A Capability Statement outlining why the respondent believes its firm has the capability to meet all these requirements outlined within Attachment 1: McMurdo PENGUIN Ground Stations - Statement of Work Relevant Past Performance Experience. Evidence of past performance of requirements similar in size, scope, and complexity. Conflict of Interest: Please detail the extent to which the respondent is aware of any potential organizational conflict of interest (actual or perceived) issues related to this requirement. Response Format: In order to better assist in the review of responses to this Sources Sough Notice, respondents are encouraged to prepare a capabilities statement that closely adheres to the following format: The document format shall be either Microsoft Word (.doc or .docx) format, or Adobe Acrobat (.pdf) format that is searchable. Responses shall be prepared using 12-point font, 1-inch margins, and 8.5-inch by 11-inch paper and shall not exceed fifteen (15) pages in length, including images, data displays, charts, graphs, and tables. SUBMISSION DEADLINE AND ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: The responses received will assist the Government with identifying the number and nature of the entities that consider themselves feasible technical solution providers. Respondents are encouraged to ensure that their responses are complete and address all items outlined within this Sources Sought Notice. This Sources Sought Notice does not constitute a commitment, implied or otherwise, that a procurement action will be issued. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable government regulations. Any material received will be considered to be public domain unless clearly marked (on each page) as proprietary. The Government will not be liable for or suffer any consequential damages for proprietary information not properly identified. title: Request for Interested Manufacturers of 6130-01-523-3338 Power Control Module (PCM) and 1095-01-523-5767 High Bandwith Assembly (HBA) for the Bomb Release Unit (BRU)-57
description: SUBJECT Market research is being conducted to identify potential sources that may possess the expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet the requirements for qualification and production of the Power Control Module (PCM), NSN 6130-01-523-3338, Part Number MT57M1177-1 and High Bandwith Assembly (HBA), NSN 1095-01-523-5767, Part Number MT57M1165-1. ITEM DESCRIPTION The PCM and HBA are components of the BRU-57/A (BRU- Bomb Release Unit) Smart Bomb Rack used on the F-16 Fighter. The PCM serves as the primary electrical power management, conditioning, and distribution hub for the BRU-57/A Smart Bomb Rack system. The HBA is the communication link for the BRU-57 bomb rack. It routes high-speed data between the F-16 and two smart weapons. The BRU-57/A PCM and HBA were developed specifically for use on the F-16 C/D aircraft with military unique requirements. The BRU-57/A is a MIL-STD-1760 capable, multiple-carriage, vertical-ejection Bomb Rack. The BRU-57/A provides side-by-side carriage and release of two 14-inch suspension stores. IMPEDIMENT TO COMPETITION The original equipment manufacturer for this item is L3Harris (CAGE 82340) previously EDO LLC. The Government does not own any data, drawings, schematics, or any other releasable technical data in support of this requirement. As a result, L3Harris is the only known source with adequate knowledge of the BRU-57 performance requirements and possession of the required technical data and capabilities needed to produce these items and ensure compatibility of the equipment. INTEREST The DLA/AWB Contracting Office intends to award a sole source contract to L3 Harris for the manufacture of the BRU-57 PCM and HBA in support of the F-16C/D program. Other interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement no later than 20 October 2026, 1700 EST by emailing robert.berg.9@us.af.mil. The Government intends to procure these items using Other Than Full and Open Competition as prescribed by RFO 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. title: McMurdo PENGUIN Ground Station Antennas and Radomes
description: INTRODUCTION SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is issued for information and market research planning purposes; it does not constitute a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) is not seeking proposals at this time, but strictly the information requested, herein. Requests for a solicitation or proposals sent in response to this notice will not receive a response. Furthermore, those who respond to this SSN should not anticipate feedback with regards to its submission. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. The information provided in this SSN is subject to change and does not bind the Government to any future obligations. All submissions become the property of the Government and will not be returned. SUMMARY OF SCOPE The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service (NESDIS), under the Office of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Observations and the Near Earth Orbit Network (NEON) / NOAA Antenna as a Service (NAaaS) program, is seeking industry capabilities and feedback regarding the procurement, fabrication, factory integration, testing, packaging, and sustainment of (5) receive-only satellite ground station systems for the PENGUIN Ground Stations project at McMurdo Station, Antarctica. See Attachment 1: McMurdo PENGUIN Ground Stations - Statement of Work for detailed scope of work information. PENGUIN Ground Station Overview Within NESDIS, the Office of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Observations maintains long-standing partnerships that support the acquisition, transport, processing, and distribution of environmental satellite data. These partnerships include cooperation with the European Organization for the Exploitation of Meteorological Satellites under the JPSS Program and are expected to expand to support the European Organization for the Exploitation of Meteorological Satellites (EUMETSAT) Polar System Second Generation (EPS-SG) constellation of microwave sounders. McMurdo Station, Antarctica, provides a strategic high-latitude location for polar-orbiting satellite data acquisition. At approximately 77.8 degrees south latitude, McMurdo enables frequent access to polar-orbiting satellites and supports Stored Mission Data downlink opportunities for NOAA and partner mission satellites. Additional receive-only ground station capability at McMurdo is required to maintain continuity, resiliency, and growth capability for NOAA environmental data acquisition architecture. The Sterna L-band mission baseline includes Stored Mission Data (SMD) reception. The delivered antenna system is expected to include installed L-, S-, and X-band receive hardware capability. NOAA/NAaaS will establish S-band and X-band performance and interface specifications to support future mission requirements; these parameters are identified in the procurement technical specification. description: Request For Information C-130 Corrosion Prevention and Control Program (CPCP) Sustaining Engineering and Technical Support Services This Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Synopsis is issued solely for informational, market research, and planning purposes pursuant to FAR Part 10. The Government anticipates pursuing a sole-source contract. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or solicitation, nor does it represent a commitment or authorization to incur costs on behalf of the United States Government (USG). The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the repair data, expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualification requirements to conduct C-130 Corrosion Prevention and Control Program (CPCP). Corrosion prevention and control is defined as the rigorous application of management principles, engineering design and analysis, quality assurance, nondestructive inspection, manufacturing, operations and support technologies, and practices to prevent the initiation of corrosion, avoid functional impairment due to corrosion, and define processes for the tracking and repair of corrosion problems. The Contractor shall provide sustaining engineering and technical support for the C-130 CPCP for the C-130 Hercules Division (AFLCMC/WLN) at Robins Air Force Base (AFB), GA. The Contractor shall provide engineering and technical support for the strategic planning and oversight of the corrosion program and the ASIP requirements of MIL-STD-1530D. Services include engineering and technical analysis, providing guidance for corrective action, and providing documentation as required for the prevention, control and resolution of corrosion related issues on C-130 aircraft: Developing and providing annual updates to the C-130 Corrosion Prevention and Control (CPC) Plan Conducting annual corrosion assessments of USAF C-130 fleet and operating locations, including evaluation of aircraft, facilities, and maintenance personnel, to include Special Operations Forces (SOF) managed C-130s Performing concept studies and analysis in the identification and definition, preliminary planning, and evaluation of alternative technical approaches for all USAF C-130 aircraft Conducting concept studies and testing for implementation of new coatings, sealants, or other corrosion related products and processes, including test plan development and final report delivery with findings and recommendations to the USAF Contractors/Institutions responding to this market research are placed on notice that participation in this survey may not ensure participation in future solicitations or contract awards. title: Request for Information/Market Intelligence Notice: Multiple Projects at Vandenberg Space Force Base - Use of Progressive Design Build (PDB) with Other Transaction Authority (OTA)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE: This is a request for information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a solicitation or a request for proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS CODE: 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction 237130 Power and Communication Line and Related Structures Construction SMALL BUSINESS STANDARD: $45,000,000.00 NOTE: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR based small business regulations, these NAICS codes are provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base. PROGRAM/PROJECT OVERVIEW: The 30th Contracting Squadron has multiple infrastructure repair and construction projects planned in Fiscal Year 2027 including heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) repair, secure facility renovation, medium-high voltage electrical distribution line repair/replacement, airfield lighting repair, fitness track repair/replacement, and road repair/construction, fire alarm and elevator repair/replacement. The Government is evaluating the feasibility of executing these requirements via Progressive Design-Build (PDB) utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a in conjunction with the United States Space Force (USSF) Construction Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) at https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/68c3d9f987984f448cd067abaf2950d0/view. Summaries of potential projects being considered for this acquisition strategy are as follows: HVAC Repair: Design and construct the repair and replacement of the HVAC for a multi-tenant office building. Secure Facility Renovation: Design and construction of renovations of a secure facility to meet revised mission requirements Renovation is expected to include wall relocation, electrical, communications, HVAC, and associated finished associated with a facility renovation. Medium-High Voltage Electrical Distribution: Design and construction of the replacement of an aged electrical distribution system ranging from 15kV to 70kV. Airfield Repair: Investigate, design, and construct repairs to various airfield infrastructure to bring it up to current FAA and military airfield code and standards. Outdoor Fitness Track Repair/Replacement: Design and construct repairs to stabilize the soil conditions and repair failing rubberized track surface. Road Repair/Construction: Design and construct road repairs to stabilize subsurface conditions and improve roadways to meet increasing haul capacity and traffic. Fire Suppression and Elevator Repair/Replacement: Design and construct the replacement of a freight elevator for personnel and freight access and the replacement of the existing fire alarm system to include connectivity with the new elevator. INFORMATION REQUESTED: Interested industry partners are requested to respond to the following questions to help shape the final acquisition strategy: Company Profile: Q1. Business Name Q2. Address Q3. Point of Contract (Name, Title) Q4. Phone Number Q5. Email Address Q6. Unique Entity ID Q7. Cage Code Q8. Socioeconomic Status (Other Than Small, Small, 8(a), SDVOSB, etc.) Q9. Participating Role (Prime Contractor, Subcontractor, Design Firm, Other) Q10: Which of the seven (7) projects your company may be interested in responding to if the projects are issued as PDB OT Agreements. Please select from one of the following: No experience Limited Experience (1 � 5 projects completed) Very Experienced (5+ projects completed) Q12. What project characteristics make PDB OTA particularly advantageous or disadvantageous for these requirements Progressive Design-Build (PDB) / Early Contractor Involvement: Q13. What minimum level of detail (e.g., Statement of Need, conceptual site plans, target budget) does your firm require prior to submitting a White Paper (Executive Summary, Outline of proposed construction method, estimated schedule, Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) price)? Q14. What minimum level of detail (e.g., Statement of Need, conceptual site plans, target budget) does your firm require prior to a Phase 1 award (Design/Pre-construction) to feel confident in the project's viability? Q15. What collaborative mechanisms (such as joint design charrettes, target-value design workshops, or phased scoping approvals) do you recommend the Government implement in the first 30-90 days to rapidly transition from a "blank page" to a mutually agreed-upon baseline? Q16. Describe your experience executing Progressive Design-Build, Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR), or other highly collaborative delivery methods where designer and builder worked collaboratively with the owner before locking in a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). Q17. Which of the following levels of designs would be the lowest level at which you would feel confident negotiating a GMP? Charrette (basic concept, floor plans, little to no engineering review completed) 35% Design (charrette documentation plus design narrative completed, list of projected codes, UFCs, and disciplines, initial site visit completed by engineering team) 65% Design (35% design documentation plus design analysis including investigation report, explanation of major design decisions, list of specifications, engineering data, environmental surveys) 95% Design (65% design brought to 100% design level except for administrative corrections and engineering stamps) 100% Design (100% complete signed and stamped drawings issued for construction) Feedback on the Acquisition Strategy & Alternatives: Q18. Does the proposed PDB-OTA strategy incentivize your firm to participate? Why or why not? Q19. Are there alternative acquisition strategies, commercial phasing arrangements, or risk-sharing terms that the Government has not considered that would yield a higher quality facility, faster delivery, or lower cost? Bonding Capability: Q20. Specify your maximum bonding (single and aggregate) as a sole prime contractor and/or as a joint venture. Upon completion of industry feedback and market intelligence the Government may or may issue a USSF CSO Area of Interest for one, some, all, or none of the projects.
